Lehmann, who demonstrated his chainsaw carving skills at the Carman Country Fair this summer, says the response since then has been overwhelming. That connection became particularly meaningful as Lehmann learned more about the symbolism associated with the eagle feather and other elements of Indigenous culture. world.desc: MOGADISHU — Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre has chaired the first meeting of the National Disaster Risk Management Committee, which reviewed the country’s drought situation and concerns over potential severe flooding as the Deyr rains are expected to begin in parts of Somalia. The Prime Minister directed the committee to intensify public awareness on flood risks, particularly for communities living near rivers and waterways, while strengthening emergency response and coordinating relief efforts. The committee presented updates on disaster preparedness, emergency response plans and public awareness campaigns targeting communities in low-lying and flood-prone areas. Somalia is highly vulnerable to climate-related disasters, including droughts and floods, which have repeatedly displaced communities, damaged infrastructure and worsened food insecurity. According to the World Food Programme’s latest Country Brief for August 2026, one third of Somalia’s population, six million people, is facing acute hunger or worse, including nearly two million people in emergency levels of hunger. WFP requires USD 198 million for the next six months but faces an urgent shortfall of USD 147 million. Preparing for the Deyr Rains and El Niño The meeting comes as authorities prepare for the upcoming Deyr rainy season, traditionally one of Somalia’s two main rainy periods. The latest climate forecasts point to a dangerous outlook: prolonged dry conditions through October, followed by an elevated risk of El Niño-related flooding before the end of the year. At a time when households are already struggling with weak purchasing power and repeated shocks, flooding could further disrupt livelihoods, markets and food access. The Minister of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation, Ali Yusuf (Ali Xoosh), has warned the Somali public about the risk of floods and flash floods linked to the anticipated Super El Niño weather phenomenon, urging communities to take precautionary measures and remain vigilant. The launch comes as government intensifies efforts to halt illegal mining, and close unlicensed mines across the country.
